title: Ernie Jr.'s dispute with Bobby Bland's management
summary: Junior led Bobby Bland's band, sued over unpaid money and hit union and management complications; Fields wishes he had taught him the union ways.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: One thing you talk about the union, that is where (inaudible), that's one time I wish I trained Ernie, Jr. along those lines.

Bobby owed him a quite a bit of money, but he was making enough that he could pay his men and he paid his men. I told him, always pay your musicians. Well now, if he hadn't of done that, I know they would have had to win the case, because everything would (inaudible).
Every musician would
have filed against him.
That's it exactly. So when he came to that and filed for that, they never did give a rebuttal, and won the case.
Bobby Bland did?

No. That's when he turned and said, the hell with the union and this and that and so on and really, Marla (phonetic spelling) got on the case and my secretary--he belonged to both of them--it's not even over now--one guy is a lobbyist for the union, although it doesn't look like our lobbyist is going to do a darn thing, is on the case. They think it was a payoff some kind of way.
We're not saying that he was right, Ernie Fields had to win, but how could he win and denounce him.
Ernie is a little more sharper on a lot of things in business and a young man, you might say to me, he has a little deal that

whenever he does anything business, he's making a tape. But at that time he didn't have it on. Evelyn Johnson called him and said, Junior, (inaudible) I don't want to be bothered with all this, so let's come to some kind of compromise. And he said, Evelyn, it's too much money for that, he said let's think out something. She went on and anyway, he went on and filed it and everything was cut and dry, just like I told you this bandleader did in Tulsa about that deal, and he got one answer that the band was on the road and as soon as they could catch them, they will. So you have two weeks to answer anyway, and sure, he ain't heard nothing (inaudible).
Evelyn Johnson runs the--what do you call the agency--Buffalo?
Yeah.
And she books Bobby Bland. She still does?
No, no. ABC bought the contract.
Oh, so Evelyn's not involved with Bobby Bland?
Not now, not no more.
But she was then?
She was then, that's why she was pleading with Ernie, Jr. not to do it.
Yeah, because Don Roby's dead and she was the sole booker.
No, she wasn't sole booker, she was--ABC was booking him then, but she became the personal manager of Bobby Bland.
Well, there's a good chance Ernie might win the case, but--
